feat(sessions): add support for remote redis session store (#3345)

Description
====================
zot currently stores session cookies in memory or in a local directory.
For cases where the session cookies should be independent of the
instance where they were created such as multiple instances of zot, or a
fully stateless zot instance, there is a need to support a remote
session storage.
This change adds support for using Redis and Redis-compatible services as a
remote session driver as well as introduces a new configuration option
for it.

What has changed
=======================
- New config added under Auth config to specify configuration for
  the session driver.
- Examples README updated with details of the new Auth config.
- The config supports only 2 drivers in this change - local and redis
- Using the local driver is backwards compatible and behaves the same
  way that zot currently works for local session storage.
- Omitting this config does not result in an error. In this case, zot
  behaves as it normally does for local session storage.
- When configured, zot can use redis for persisting cookie
  information for zot UI.
- The cookie in the store is deleted on logout or after the max
  expiry time for the cookie.
- Configuration for the redis session driver accepts the same configuration
  values as that of the remote meta cache.
- A separate connection is established for the session driver. An
  existing connection for meta cache will not be re-used for the
  session driver.
- A key prefix is configurable for the redis session driver. The value will be
  converted into a string for use. If no value is provided, a default
  prefix of "zotsession" will be used.
- Redis sessions does not support hash key or encryption in this change.
- New BATS test added to verify zot behavior with Redis session store.
- Github workflow updated to install valkey-tools dependency for BATS.

Signed-off-by: Vishwas Rajashekar <dev@vrajashkr.com>

feat: the default retention delay is not the GC delay (#3447)

Most users don't make the difference between retention deleting untagged manifests vs GC deleting other blobs.
This causes confusion since the GC delay and the retention delay (used for untagged manifests and orphan referrers) have different defaults, and are set separately in the zot configuration.
Most users don't configrue retention policies, and they still expect untagged manifests to be deleted at GC time.

With this change, if retention delay is not specified in the config file, the value used is the GC delay.
If GC delay is also unspecified in the config file, the default GC delay is used for both.

fix: migrate to Go module v2 for proper semantic versioning (#3462)

* fix: migrate to Go module v2 for proper semantic versioning

This change updates the module path from 'zotregistry.dev/zot' to
'zotregistry.dev/zot/v2' to comply with Go's semantic versioning rules.

According to Go's module versioning requirements, major version v2+
must include the major version in the module path. The current
module path 'zotregistry.dev/zot' only supports v0.x.x and v1.x.x
versions, making existing v2.x.x tags (like v2.1.8) unusable.

Changes:
- Updated go.mod module path to zotregistry.dev/zot/v2
- Updated all internal import paths across 280+ Go source files
- Updated configuration files (golangcilint.yaml, gqlgen.yml)
- Updated README.md Go reference badge

This fix enables proper use of existing v2.x.x Git tags and allows
external packages to import zot v2+ versions without compatibility
errors.

Resolves: Go module import compatibility for v2+ versions
Fixes: #3071
Signed-off-by: Luca Muscariello <muscariello@ieee.org>

* fix: regenerate GraphQL files with updated v2 import paths

The gqlgen tool needs to regenerate the GraphQL schema files after
the module path change to use the new v2 imports.

Signed-off-by: Luca Muscariello <muscariello@ieee.org>

fix: configure cookie Secure flag based on TLS configuration (#3482)

Make the Secure flag for session cookies configurable based on Zot's
TLS settings. This allows cookies to work properly when Zot is
accessed over HTTP (without TLS).

Changes:
- Add SecureSession field to AuthConfig to allow explicit control
- Add UseSecureSession() method that returns true when TLS is
  configured, or uses SecureSession setting if provided
- Update saveUserLoggedSession() to accept and use secure parameter
- Add tests for UseSecureSession() in config_test.go
- Enhance authn tests to verify cookie Secure flag behavior
- Fix TestAuthnSessionErrors by creating new client without cookies

The logic is:
- If TLS is configured, cookies always have Secure=true
- If TLS is not configured but SecureSession is explicitly set,
  use that value
- Otherwise, default to Secure=false for HTTP-only deployments

Signed-off-by: Andrei Aaron <andreifdaaron@gmail.com>

feat: add zot subcommand to enable testing retention policy settings (#3449)

feat: add verify-feature retention subcommand with comprehensive testing and validation

Add a `verify-feature retention` subcommand that allows users to preview and
validate retention policy changes without running the actual Zot server.
The command runs GC and retention tasks in dry-run mode for immediate feedback.

- Run verify-feature retention standalone without starting the server
- Preview retention policy decisions in dry-run mode
- Configurable GC interval override via command-line flag
- Optional timeout for task completion
- Configurable log output (stdout or file)

Basic usage:
```bash
zot verify-feature retention <config-file>
```

With log file output:
```bash
zot verify-feature retention -l /var/log/zot-retention-check.log <config-file>
```

With GC interval override (runs GC tasks every 30 seconds):
```bash
zot verify-feature retention -i 30s <config-file>
```

With timeout (wait up to 5 minutes for tasks to complete):
```bash
zot verify-feature retention -t 5m <config-file>
```

Combined flags:
```bash
zot verify-feature retention -l /var/log/zot-retention-check.log -i 1m -t 10m <config-file>
```

The command supports overriding GC settings from the config:
- `-i, --gc-interval`: Override the GC interval setting (applies to all storage paths including subpaths)

- Refactored `RunGCTasks` from `controller.go` to be reusable
- Added `checkServerRunning` validation to prevent conflicts
- Implemented signal handling for graceful shutdown
- Added configuration sanitization and logging
- Set GCMaxSchedulerDelay programmatically (not user-configurable)

Added tests for coverage on main function:
- Negative test cases (no args, bad config, GC disabled, server running)
- Both BoltDB and Redis
- Retention enabled scenarios with complex image setups
- Retention disabled scenarios
- Delete referrers functionality
- Subpaths configuration
- GC interval override validation

Run the verify-feature retention tests:
```bash
go test -v ./pkg/cli/server -run TestRetentionCheck
```

Signed-off-by: Andrei Aaron <andreifdaaron@gmail.com>

fix(meta): handle cases when substores are nested (#3598)

fix(meta): handle cases where repositories when substores are nested

Note this is a case of bad configuration: having multiple stores
in the same tree structure. Guard against it in parse.go.

Fix getAllRepos to prevent duplicate repositories in metaDB when substore
directories are nested under the default store root directory.

The fix processes substores first, then the default store, using a
map-based deduplication approach to skip repositories that have already
been added. This ensures that when both the default store and substores
contain repositories with the same name (e.g., when a substore is nested
within the default store), only one instance is added to the repository
list.

Add test TestNoDuplicateReposWithSubstoresAndNestedRepoNames to verify
the deduplication logic works correctly with nested substores.

Also update the other tests to avoid these issues in the future
this is not a vali configuration.

This is not the intended use case for substores, and it may have caused:
https://github.com/project-zot/zot/actions/runs/19665302669/job/56320640980

end of successful execution paths, which could lead to incorrect error
handling when 'err' was overwritten in loops or conditionals.

Changed the following functions to return nil explicitly when all
operations succeed:

- SearchTags: return nil instead of err after successful loop
- GetRepoMeta: return nil instead of err after successful operations

This commit fixes a critical bug where RemoveImageFromRepoMeta crashes with
a nil pointer dereference during retention policy execution and GC operations.

Root Cause:
The function was accessing blob metadata without checking if it exists first.
During GC/retention operations, the metadata database might have stale
references to blobs that no longer exist, causing runtime panics.

Changes:
- Added nil check for descriptorBlobInfo before accessing LastUpdated field
- Added nil check for blobInfo before dereferencing Size, Vendors, Platforms, and SubBlobs
- Made the function consistent with recalculateAggregateFields which already had these checks

Impact:
- Fixes crashes during retention policy execution
- Fixes crashes during GC manifest removal
- Fixes image deletion failures via API
- Eliminates need for dryRun: true workaround in retention config

The fix gracefully handles missing blob metadata by skipping those entries
instead of crashing.

ResetRepoReferences would clear all tags, causing timestamp information to
be lost and reset to the service restart time for existing images.

This change adds TaggedTimestamp support and modifies ResetRepoReferences to
selectively preserve tags that still exist in storage, maintaining their
TaggedTimestamp values. Tags that no longer exist in storage are removed as
before.

Changes:
- Add TaggedTimestamp field to GraphQL ImageSummary schema
- Update GraphQL conversion functions to populate TaggedTimestamp with
  fallback to PushTimestamp when unavailable
- Updated ResetRepoReferences interface to accept tagsToKeep parameter
- Modified ParseRepo to collect tags from storage before resetting
- Updated all backend implementations (Redis, DynamoDB, BoltDB) to preserve
  tags in tagsToKeep instead of clearing all tags
- Updated tests and mocks to match new signature

This ensures TaggedTimestamp accurately reflects when tags were originally
created, and exposes this information through the GraphQL API.

Pin actions and tighten workflow permissions (#3954)

* ci: Reduce chance of installing corrupt packages

See: https://dev.to/hsbt/should-rubygemsbundler-have-a-cooldown-feature-40cp
Signed-off-by: Benoit Tigeot <benoit.tigeot@lifen.fr>

* ci: prevent credential leakage from checkout steps

Add `persist-credentials: false` to all `actions/checkout` calls across
22 workflow files. Without this, the GitHub token used for checkout is
written into `.git/config` and remains accessible to all subsequent steps
and any uploaded artifacts (artipacked finding).

Signed-off-by: Benoit Tigeot <benoit.tigeot@lifen.fr>

* ci: prevent template injection from github context in run steps

`${{ github.* }}` expressions used directly inside `run:` blocks are
expanded before the shell sees them. A crafted value (e.g. a tag name
containing shell metacharacters) would execute arbitrary code.

Move the values into `env:` variables (e.g. GITHUB_EVENT_RELEASE_TAG_NAME,
GITHUB_ACTOR) and reference them as `${VAR}` in the shell, so the runtime
never interprets them as code (template-injection finding).

Signed-off-by: Benoit Tigeot <benoit.tigeot@lifen.fr>

* ci: prevent injection in yq commands via release tag name

`${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}` was interpolated directly into
yq `cmd:` inputs. A crafted tag name could inject shell commands since
the expression is expanded before the action runs. Use yq's `strenv()`
with an `env:` variable instead so the value is always treated as data.

Signed-off-by: Benoit Tigeot <benoit.tigeot@lifen.fr>

* ci: pin all GitHub Actions to full commit SHAs

Actions pinned to mutable tags (e.g. @v6, @main) can change under us if
the upstream repo is compromised or tags are moved, enabling supply-chain
attacks. Pinning to the full 40-char commit SHA locks the exact code that
runs. Version tags are preserved as inline comments (e.g. # v6.0.2) for
readability and Dependabot compatibility.

Used `pinact` for standard tagged versions; remaining branch-based
references (mikefarah/yq, jlumbroso/free-disk-space,
project-stacker/stacker-build-push-action, aquasecurity/trivy-action)
resolved manually via the GitHub API.

Signed-off-by: Benoit Tigeot <benoit.tigeot@lifen.fr>

* ci: slow down GitHub Actions dependency updates to biweekly

Dependabot has no native biweekly interval. Combining weekly checks with
a 14-day cooldown achieves the same effect: Dependabot scans every Monday
but won't open a PR for a new action version until 14 days after release,
giving the ecosystem time to stabilize before we adopt it.

Signed-off-by: Benoit Tigeot <benoit.tigeot@lifen.fr>

* ci: group all Dependabot updates into single PRs per ecosystem

Without groups, Dependabot opens one PR per dependency. With `patterns: "*"`,
all Go module bumps land in one PR and all GitHub Actions pin updates in
another, reducing review noise.

Signed-off-by: Benoit Tigeot <benoit.tigeot@lifen.fr>

* ci: restore credential persistence for helm-charts push

`persist-credentials: false` was too broad — the helm-charts checkout
uses HELM_PUSH_TOKEN specifically so the subsequent `git push` can
authenticate. Only the main repo checkout should have credentials disabled.

* ci: use --password-stdin for oras login

Passing the token via `-p` exposes it in process listings and debug

fix(auth): add workaround for Docker client auth with mixed anonymous policies (#3868)

* fix(auth): add workaround for Docker client auth with mixed anonymous policies

Docker client fails to authenticate to protected repositories when basic auth
(htpasswd/LDAP) is used with mixed access policies (some repos anonymous,
some requiring auth). This happens because Docker determines whether to send
credentials based on the /v2/ response - if it returns 200, Docker assumes
no auth is needed anywhere.

Add `forceDockerClientAuth` config option that, when enabled, forces 401 on
/v2/ for Docker clients, triggering Docker's authentication flow.

This workaround only affects Docker clients (detected via User-Agent).
Podman and other OCI-compliant clients are unaffected.

Refs: https://github.com/opencontainers/wg-auth/blob/main/docs/implementations/moby.md

fix(api): recognize Docker Compose/Buildx User-Agent in v2 challenge workaround (#3992)

Docker Compose and Buildx proxy through the Docker daemon, which sends
a User-Agent starting with "docker/<version>" rather than the
"Docker-Client/<version>" string sent by direct Docker CLI pulls.
This caused compose/buildx pulls to skip the 401 challenge on
registries with mixed anonymous/authenticated access policies,
resulting in 'unauthorized' errors.

Add strings.HasPrefix(ua, "docker/") alongside the existing
Docker-Client check so daemon-proxied requests from any upstream
tool (compose, buildx, etc.) are handled correctly.

feat(auth): support OIDC RP-Initiated Logout (#3975)

POST /zot/auth/logout now returns an endSessionUrl in the JSON
response body when the session was established via an OIDC provider
whose discovery document advertises an endSessionEndpoint, so the
UI can navigate the browser to it and terminate the session at the
IdP in addition to clearing the local cookie.

- The OIDC callback records the provider name in the session after
  login; the github OAuth2 path is untouched.
- end_session_endpoint is read from the zitadel/oidc RelyingParty
  and validated as an absolute http(s) URL.
- post_logout_redirect_uri prefers http.externalUrl when set and
  falls back to deriving the origin from the incoming request.
- No id_token_hint is sent; client_id identifies the RP, so the
  ID token does not need to be persisted.
- Non-OIDC sessions (local/basic/LDAP/GitHub) retain the existing
  200 OK, no body behavior.

Operators must register the URI zot sends as a valid post-logout
redirect URI on the IdP client.

Ref: https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-rpinitiated-1_0.html

Multipart download enhancements (#4021)

* fix(api): set blob response Content-Type from OCI descriptor

Blob HEAD responses had no Content-Type and GET responses echoed the
request's Accept header verbatim, which produced missing or malformed
media types and left multipart/byteranges parts without a per-part
Content-Type. This breaks OCI distribution-spec conformance and
consumers like stargz-snapshotter that need a well-formed layer media
type.

Add a blobResponseMediaType helper that resolves the descriptor's
MediaType via GetBlobDescriptorFromRepo and falls back to
application/octet-stream. Use it in CheckBlob (HEAD), GetBlob full
(200), GetBlob single-range (206), and per-part in
writeMultipartRanges (206 multipart). Lookup is deferred until after
the blob is known to exist.

Cover the new behaviour with mock-based unit tests in routes_test.go
and end-to-end assertions in TestPullRange.

Signed-off-by: Andrei Aaron <andreifdaaron@gmail.com>

* perf(api): stream multipart blob ranges lazily with precomputed Content-Length

writeMultipartRanges previously opened every range reader up front
and emitted no Content-Length, so an N-range request held N
concurrent storage readers (and their fds / read buffers) per
response window and forced chunked encoding on HTTP/1.1 — neither
friendly to proxies nor to fan-out scenarios like stargz lazy pulls.

Signed-off-by: Andrei Aaron <andreifdaaron@gmail.com>

ci: fix golangci-lint install URL (#4052)

1. Cause
SBOM assets were added to the release checksum file, so you get two lines that contain the same substring, e.g. …linux-amd64.tar.gz and …linux-amd64.tar.gz.sbom.json.
The old install.sh logic used something like grep "${BASENAME}", so both lines matched. That breaks want (wrong or ambiguous hash) and shows up as checksum verification errors (including the 8df… vs fd3… style mismatch you debugged).

2. The upstream fix is in https://github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/pull/6539
The matcher was changed so the checksum line must end with the archive name — i.e. grep "${BASENAME}$" — so the .sbom.json line no longer matches.

3. In the same thread they say master on raw.githubusercontent.com is not the right branch anymore and recommend the canonical installer URL:
https://golangci-lint.run/install.sh
(see the PR description and local install / binaries.)

Signed-off-by: Andrei Aaron <andreifdaaron@gmail.com>

fix(storage): treat dedupe-candidate cache miss as no candidates, not an error (#4122)

GetAllDedupeReposCandidates propagated zerr.ErrCacheMiss from the cache's
GetAllBlobs verbatim. But a cache miss is the normal case for a not-yet-cached
blob — the first push of a new blob, or a cross-repo mount check during a push
— and semantically means "no dedupe/mount candidates", not a failure.

Propagating it caused canMount (used by the CheckBlob and CreateBlobUpload
handlers) to surface the error, which the route handlers log as an
"unexpected error". With remote (e.g. S3) storage a cache is always present
(dedupe:false does not disable it), so this logs an error-level line for every
fresh blob digest on every push — significant log spam during bulk pushes and
cross-repo mounts, with no functional impact (the push still succeeds via a
normal upload).

Handle ErrCacheMiss the same way as the existing nil-cache branch above:
return no candidates and no error.

Signed-off-by: Janko Thyson <janko@kaosmaps.com>

fix(storage): normalize repository names to '/' separators on Windows (#4188)

filepath.Rel returns OS-specific separators, so on Windows the repo
walkers (GetRepositories, GetNextRepository, GetNextRepositories)
produced backslash-separated names such as 'openshift4\ose-cli'. Those
names fail FullNameRegexp validation in ValidateRepo, which only
accepts '/' as a component separator, so every namespaced repository
was silently dropped. As a result /v2/_catalog returned an empty list,
and garbage collection, scrub, and metadb never saw any repositories.

Convert each relative path with filepath.ToSlash (a no-op on Unix)
before validation, matching the existing ToSlash usage elsewhere in
imagestore.go.

Digest-only pull-through cache entries are stored as untagged manifests, so existing tag-based retention rules do not protect actively pulled content. This adds explicit untagged retention rules that use the same pull/push activity signals as tag retention.

  "deleteUntagged": true,
  "keepTags": [{

Builds untagged candidates from index descriptors without tag annotations.
Joins candidates with MetaDB digest statistics.
Evaluates tag and untagged pools independently.
Garbage collection

Skips untagged manifests retained by keepUntagged.
Falls back to existing delay-based cleanup when untagged retention cannot use MetaDB statistics.

fix(storage): defer blob deletes for cache-unknown blobs until dedupe rebuild completes (#4195)

With dedupe enabled on cloud storage, duplicate blobs are stored as
zero-size placeholders whose content lives in a single original blob,
resolvable only through the dedupe cache. When the cache is lost or
incomplete (e.g. an ephemeral local cache database with cloud storage),
deleteBlob's cache lookup misses, the move-content-to-next-duplicate
logic is skipped entirely, and the storage delete destroys the only
content-bearing copy. Every duplicate of that digest in other
repositories is then permanently broken (416 RequestedRangeNotSatisfiable
on read), which is the data loss reported in issue #2625.

The startup dedupe/restore walk (RunDedupeBlobs) already rebuilds the
cache from storage, but GC/retention can run before or while it does,
which is exactly the corruption window.

Fix: track completion of the dedupe/restore walk on the ImageStore
(reusing the DedupeTaskGenerator completion callback, renamed to
OnRunComplete and now fired for both dedupe and restore runs) and
defer deletes of content-bearing blobs that the cache cannot account
for until the walk has completed. Such deletes
return the new ErrDedupeRebuildInProgress; GC/retention retries on a
later interval, and blobs known to the cache (or zero-size
placeholders) are unaffected. Local storage is exempt: it dedupes via
hardlinks, so deleting one path never destroys shared content.

The gate is armed only when RunDedupeBlobs is invoked (the server
always does at startup), so stores that never schedule the walk keep
existing behavior. Generator submission order in StartBackgroundTasks
is deliberately unchanged: the walk being scheduled a few statements
after the GC generator leaves only a sub-millisecond arming window,
whereas reordering the submissions shifts the GC generator's first
pass by a scheduler slot and changes long-standing GC timing behavior.

Fixes #2625

Signed-off-by: Johnathan Aretos <johnathan@squareup.com>

feat(sync): add oauth2 credential helper for JWT assertion exchange #4146 (#4147)

* feat(sync): add oauth2 credential helper for JWT assertion exchange

Add an in-process "oauth2" credential helper for the sync extension that
exchanges a JWT assertion (for example a Kubernetes projected service
account token) for a short-lived registry access token via an OAuth2 token
endpoint. This supports upstream registries that only allow token-based
authentication with short-lived credentials, without depending on an
external docker credential helper binary, keeping zot's single distroless
binary deployment model intact.

The helper follows the existing ECR helper pattern: it implements the
CredentialHelper interface and is selected via "credentialHelper": "oauth2"
with options provided in the new credentialHelperConfig block. Both the
client_credentials (client_assertion) and jwt-bearer grant types are
supported, and tokens are cached and refreshed before expiry.

fix(sync): predict post-OCI digest for on-demand skip checks (#4185)

* fix(sync): predict post-OCI digest for on-demand skip checks

On-demand sync compares the locally stored digest (after regclient
mod.WithManifestToOCI at commit time) with the remote digest in
CanSkipImage. For Docker images such as registry.k8s.io/pause:3.10.1,
the upstream manifest-list digest differs from the post-conversion OCI
index digest.

The previous hand-rolled convertDockerManifestToOCI /
convertDockerListToOCI logic in remote.go did not match regclient's
conversion (including WithManifestToOCIReferrers and hybrid indexes),
so GetOCIDigest returned the wrong value, skip never matched, and sync
logged "remote image digest changed, syncing again" in a loop.

Replace that with predictOCIDigest, an in-memory mirror of regclient's
manifest conversion that needs only manifest JSON (no config/layer
blobs). Skip ManifestGet for unchanged OCI platform manifests listed in
an index. Add tests against mod.Apply and document remote call counts.

Fixes the resync loop described in #4184; first-pull latency and full
layer re-downloads are separate follow-ups.

CommitAll was promoting temp ocidir entries tagged sha256-* into the
destination registry, polluting tags/list after Docker→OCI conversion.
Referrers tag names are spec-defined index transport only: skip
referrers-tagged manifests and commit child manifests from referrers
indexes without storing the index itself.

fix(storage): skip reserved dirs in GetNextRepository walk (#4227)

GetNextRepository descended into every already-processed repo's subtree,
including <repo>/.uploads/. On backends where listing an empty prefix
returns PathNotFoundError (e.g. GCS: a ghost prefix left by an abandoned
upload session), the nested List error aborted the whole walk and was
mapped to "no more repositories", so periodic GC silently stopped and
never collected any repository sorting after the poisoned one.

Add the same ErrSkipDir guard for .sync/blobs/.uploads that the sibling
walkers (GetRepositories, GetRepositoriesWithPagination) already use, so
enumeration never descends into or lists reserved directories. Covered by
a regression test that exercises the real storagedriver.WalkFallback path
used by the GCS driver.

fix(meta): derive push timestamp from blob mod time on storage parse (#4234)

* fix(meta): derive push timestamp from blob mod time on storage parse

The push timestamp only lives in the metaDB. When the metaDB is lost
(e.g. a non-persistent cache backend restarts) the storage parse
recreated every statistics entry with time.Now(), stamping all images
with the startup time. Retention policies based on push time
(pushedWithin, mostRecentlyPushedCount) then saw one identical fake
timestamp and expired every tag at the same moment.

Pass the manifest blob's storage mod time as a hint through ImageMeta
and prefer it over time.Now() when a new statistics entry is created.
On object storage blobs are immutable, so the mod time is the original
upload time and a metaDB rebuild reconstructs the real push dates.

Closes https://github.com/project-zot/zot/issues/4233

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Sebastian Thees <thees@users.noreply.github.com>

* refactor(meta): pass push timestamp hint as explicit SetRepoReference option

The blob mod time hint rode on ImageMeta, but ImageMeta is digest-global
manifest data shared across all repos referencing the digest, while the
push time is per repo and digest (DescriptorStatistics). Make the hint
an explicit variadic option on SetRepoReference so ImageMeta stays pure
manifest data. The variadic parameter keeps all existing call sites
source-compatible.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Sebastian Thees <thees@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(meta): stat manifest blob under store lock on parse

StatBlob requires the caller to hold the store lock, but the mod time
hint was gathered inside SetImageMetaFromInput, which is also reached
from the push and sync paths without any lock. Move the StatBlob call
to parseRepo, which already holds the store RLock, and pass the hint
through SetImageMetaFromInput as a SetRepoReference option. The push
and sync paths no longer stat the blob at all; they fall back to
time.Now() as before.

Also look up the manifest blob path in the parse test via the
ImageStore.BlobPath API instead of hard-coding the on-disk layout.

Addresses review comments on the PR.

fix(storage): check table existence before CreateTable in dynamodb cache (#4260)

* fix(storage): check table existence before CreateTable in dynamodb cache

The storage-cache DynamoDB driver's NewTable always called CreateTable
on startup and only tolerated the error when it happened to contain
"Table already exists" (a ResourceInUseException, returned when the
caller has CreateTable permission and the table exists). When the
caller instead lacks dynamodb:CreateTable entirely -- even with full
read/write/describe access to an existing table -- IAM denies the API
call before DynamoDB ever checks the table's existence, so the driver
got an AccessDeniedException it didn't recognize and zot failed to
start.

Add tableExists (via DescribeTable, which the caller does have
permission for) and only call CreateTable when the table is genuinely
missing, mirroring the pattern already used by the metaDB DynamoDB
driver in pkg/meta/dynamodb/dynamodb.go. Use errors.As against the
typed SDK exceptions instead of matching on err.Error() substrings.

Added an internal regression test that intercepts only the CreateTable
call against a real (localstack) DynamoDB endpoint to simulate the
IAM policy from the report, proving it fails on the old code and
passes with this fix.

Fixes https://github.com/project-zot/zot/issues/4259

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ramkumar Chinchani <rchincha.dev@gmail.com>

* fix(storage): confirm table exists before treating ResourceInUseException as benign

ResourceInUseException from CreateTable can also occur while a table is
being deleted, not just when a concurrent instance created it. Re-check
via DescribeTable so a mid-deletion race doesn't get silently ignored.

Signed-off-by: Ramkumar Chinchani <rchincha.dev@gmail.com>

NewTable previously failed outright if DescribeTable was denied, even

dynamodb:DescribeTable. Treat AccessDeniedException from DescribeTable
as "existence unknown" and fall back to CreateTable, still tolerating
ResourceInUseException. When confirming a benign ResourceInUseException

call, since a CreateTable-only caller can't perform that check either.

* feat: send an http event when an image has been scanned

Implements sending an HTTP event when Zot finishes an image scan.

Signed-off-by: Ramkumar Chinchani <rchincha.dev@gmail.com>

* fix(cve): avoid duplicate/mismatched ImageScanned events

ScanImage published an ImageScanned event on every successful call,
including cache hits: the trivy scanner returns cached results
directly without running a new scan, so repeated CVE queries (e.g.
"zli cve list") kept re-publishing the same event. It also resolved
the tag -> digest mapping after scanning, so a tag moved mid-scan
could make the event report a digest that wasn't actually scanned.

Resolve the digest up front, skip publishing when IsResultCached is
already true, and scan the resolved digest instead of the original
tag so the event always matches what was actually scanned.

Per Copilot review feedback:
- add coverage for the cache-hit and tag-move-race fixes above
- trim a comment in scan.go that just restated the code
- trim a comment in helpers_redis.bash restating a repo-wide
  convention already documented elsewhere

Also revert the gcDelay/retention.delay/sleep bump made to
garbage_collect.bats in the prior commit: per andaaron's review,
#4261 already fixes the underlying slow-push race by prefetching
images, so the wider margin isn't needed.

* fix(cve): drop named returns in resolveDigestForEvent

Signed-off-by: Ramkumar Chinchani <rchincha.dev@gmail.com>

* refactor(cve): have Scanner.ScanImage report digest/mediaType/cache status

Scanner.ScanImage now returns a ScanResult{CVEMap, Digest, MediaType,
WasCached} instead of a bare map. The trivy implementation already
resolves the scanned digest/mediaType and checks the cache internally;
surfacing that lets the event-publishing wrapper in scan.go drop every
metaDB call of its own (no more separate GetRepoMeta/GetImageMeta/
IsResultCached round trips) and just forward whatever reference the
caller passed in, trusting the underlying scanner's result.

Per andaaron's review: this also fixes the (much narrower) tag-move
race left over from the previous commit, since resolution and scanning

feat(sync): support RFC 8693 token exchange in oauth2 helper (#4269)

* feat(sync): support RFC 8693 token exchange in oauth2 helper

Add the token-exchange grant to the oauth2 sync credential helper so
that sync can obtain a short-lived registry access token from a
security token service by exchanging a subject token, rather than by
presenting a client assertion.

Three optional fields are added to the helper config and are only read
when the token-exchange grant is selected: audience, subjectTokenType
and requestedTokenType. Selecting the grant requires an audience, and
setting any of the three under another grant is rejected at load time.
Existing configurations are unaffected.

This enables Workload Identity Federation against Google Artifact
Registry with no long-lived credential on disk.

Closes #4267

Signed-off-by: frauniki <frauniki@sinoa.jp>

* docs(sync): clarify the oauth2 assertion wording and validation errors

Address review feedback. The token-exchange grant accepts subject tokens
other than JWTs, so describing the assertion as strictly a JWT was
misleading. The two new validation errors now follow the same phrasing as
the surrounding ones and name the grantType value they apply to, so a
misconfiguration points at the key to fix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: frauniki <frauniki@sinoa.jp>

* feat(sync): tighten oauth2 helper config validation

Treat a whitespace-only value as unset, so a blank tokenURL, assertion
source or audience is rejected at config load rather than sent to the
token endpoint.

Check that subjectTokenType and requestedTokenType are absolute URIs.
RFC 8693 section 3 identifies token types by URI and permits schemes
other than urn, so the scheme itself is not constrained; the check still
rejects a bare word such as "jwt". The audience is deliberately exempt:
it is a logical name rather than a URI, and the workload identity
audience Google expects carries no scheme at all.

feat(sync): add a Google Artifact Registry credential helper (#4276)

* feat(sync): add a Google Artifact Registry credential helper

The ecr helper lets an AWS user mirror from ECR with credentialHelper
alone, taking the credentials from the AWS default chain. Reaching Google
Artifact Registry needed the whole oauth2 block spelled out instead, down
to knowing that it wants the fixed username oauth2accesstoken.

Add a gcp helper built on Google application default credentials, which
covers the metadata server on GCE and GKE, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS,
an external account file for workload identity federation, and gcloud user
credentials. This needs no new dependency: golang.org/x/oauth2 is already
one, and golang.org/x/oauth2/google lives in the same module.

AreCredentialsValid asks the token source rather than comparing a fixed
window against the expiry, as the ecr helper does. The source caches a
token and mints a new one only once the old one is seconds from expiring,
so a window of its own would report the credentials expired while the
source still returned the same token, rebuilding the registry client on
every sync operation until the token finally rotated.

Closes #4275

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: frauniki <frauniki@sinoa.jp>

* test(sync): cover the gcp helper wiring and token source

Reach the paths a mock token source cannot: building the source from the
application default credentials, both when the environment names a usable
credentials file and when it does not, a token that stops being readable
after credentials were already handed out, and the service wiring for
credentialHelper "gcp".

Each of these points GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS at a file the test
controls, so none of them depends on an ambient Google credential or
reaches the network.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: frauniki <frauniki@sinoa.jp>

* fix(sync): make the gcp token source cache explicitly

Address review feedback. AreCredentialsValid is built on the token only
changing when it is really rotated, but the TokenSource interface promises
nothing about caching, so a source that minted a token per call would make
the credentials look invalid on every check and rebuild the registry
client each time. Wrap what the credentials hand back in a reusing source
so the property is guaranteed rather than assumed.

Also return early from GetCredentials when no registry was given, instead
of resolving credentials that nothing will use.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: frauniki <frauniki@sinoa.jp>

* refactor(sync): address review on the gcp credential helper

Name the two internal accessors after what they do, and drop the expiry
that gcpCredential carried but nothing ever read. With only the access
token left to remember, the struct is gone and the helper keeps a plain
map of the token handed out per registry.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: frauniki <frauniki@sinoa.jp>

* fix(sync): request the read-only scope for Google credentials

Address review feedback. The helper asked for cloud-platform, which covers
read and write across all of Google Cloud. Sync only ever pulls, so a token
that can write is a liability rather than a capability, and it widens what a
leaked token is worth.

Artifact Registry publishes only cloud-platform and this read-only form, with
nothing specific to a registry, so this is as narrow as the scope can go.

fix: dedupe digests before DynamoDB BatchGetItem (#4280)

fetchImageMetaAttributesByDigest passes the caller's digest list straight to
BatchGetItem (in chunks of AwsS3BatchLimit). DynamoDB rejects any request that
contains the same key twice with:

  api error ValidationException: Provided list of item keys contains duplicates

Repeated digests are legitimate input — several tags, or several repos, can
refer to one manifest — and the boltdb driver accepts them: FilterImageMeta
there just iterates the list and overwrites the map entry. So the same MetaDB
call succeeds on boltdb and fails on dynamodb.

The user-visible effect is that the UI home/explore page hangs on "Loading"
forever: GlobalSearch returns HTTP 200 with the DynamoDB error inside the
GraphQL body and data:null, and nothing is written to the zot log, so the
registry looks perfectly healthy. Pulls, /v2/_catalog, ExpandedRepoInfo and
Image are unaffected — they don't go through this batched path.

Query each distinct digest once. The response is expanded back to the caller's
original order and repetitions when building orderedResp, so callers (including
FilterImageMeta's len(attributes) != len(digests) check) see no behaviour
change. As a side effect the 100-key chunking now works on distinct digests, so
fewer requests are issued.

The existing "FilterImageMeta with duplicate digests" test asserted that this
returns an error, which codified the driver quirk as expected behaviour; it now
asserts the call succeeds and returns the requested digest. Verified against
amazon/dynamodb-local, which enforces the same constraint as AWS: the test
fails with the ValidationException above before this change and passes after.

This is the same class of bug as #2464, which was fixed in the image-detail
path only; #2629 later touched this function to add the 100-key chunking but
did not dedupe.

Also corrects the pre-existing comment above the chunking loop: the 100-key
limit is DynamoDB BatchGetItem's, not S3's, and the sentence was missing a
word. Flagged in review.

Signed-off-by: Sergio Fernandez <s.fernandez@docline.com>

Two issues with cosign v3 sigstore-bundle referrers:

- getCosignSignatureLayersInfo logged at error level whenever a layer
  lacked the legacy cosign signature-key annotation. Sigstore-bundle
  referrers never carry that annotation by design, so every push of one
  produced spurious error-level noise. Downgraded to debug.

- DELETE on a signature referrer could return 500 even though the
  manifest was already gone from the image store. Root cause: BoltDB's
  RemoveRepoReference clears a digest's Signatures entry as soon as its
  last tag is removed (see the "foundTag" check), even if a referrer
  manifest pointing at that digest via Subject still exists, undeleted,
  in the store. Deleting that referrer afterward then finds nothing to
  update and fails with ErrImageMetaNotFound. This is deterministic, not
  a race - delete/replace the subject's tag, then delete its signature
  referrer, and it reproduces every time (also hit internally by
  retention's own GC pass, which removes untagged manifests before
  re-checking orphaned referrers). Since the actual deletion already
  succeeded by the time this metaDB bookkeeping runs, a failure there is
  now logged but no longer turns the response into a 500.

Also fixed a copy-pasted log message in OnDeleteManifest's DeleteSignature
error branch that mislabeled this exact failure as "failed to check if
image is a signature or not", which obscured the real cause while
triaging this issue.

Tests: pkg/meta/hooks_test.go documents the metaDB-level mechanism
directly; pkg/api/routes_test.go reproduces it end to end through the
real HTTP handler (no mocked metaDB) and confirms the fix; a new
blackbox test in annotations.bats signs a real image with cosign v3,
deletes its tag, then deletes the referrer and asserts 202.

fix(imagetrust): add recognization of sigstore v3 bundles (#4307)

* fix(imagetrust): verify cosign v3 sigstore bundle signatures

cosign v3 signs with the new sigstore bundle format by default. The
signature lives inside the DSSE envelope of the bundle blob and there is
no dev.cosignproject.cosign/signature annotation, so zot had nothing to
verify against and always reported IsTrusted=false.

Verify such signatures by parsing the bundle, checking the in-toto
statement subject matches the signed manifest digest, and validating the
DSSE PAE-encoded payload against the uploaded public keys.

Fixes #4299

fix(storage): dedupe walk must visit nested-namespace repositories (#4313)

GetNextDigestWithBlobPaths pruned directories by comparing path.Base()
against the full repo paths returned by GetRepositories(). For a nested
repo such as "org/team", the walk hit "$root/org", found nothing
matching the single component "org" in repos, and returned ErrSkipDir,
so the entire nested subtree was invisible to the dedupe rebuild and
restore walks.

Consequences:
- with dedupe=true, duplicate blobs in nested repos were never
  hardlinked (local) / placeholder-linked (S3) during the startup scan,
  silently leaving the dedupe feature inert for them;
- with storage.dedupe toggled off, the restore scan skipped nested
  repos' zero-size placeholders, yet OnRunComplete still wrote the
  restore-complete marker, so the skip became permanent.

Decide whether to descend using the full relative path: descend iff the
directory is a repo itself, an ancestor of a repo, or inside a repo.
Take Andrei Aaron's review feedback: drop the now-stale long comment
that described the previous path.Base implementation, and clarify the
nolint:nilerr suppression.

Add a local-storage regression test that creates a single-level and a
nested repo sharing one blob and asserts both copies are discovered.

Signed-off-by: user.email <3349888061@qq.com>

fix(gc): collect referenced blobs once per repo during cleanup (#4236)

* fix(gc): collect referenced blobs once per repo during cleanup

CleanupRepo checked every blob against the repo index by re-reading all
manifests from storage (IsBlobReferenced per blob), making one GC run
cost O(deleted blobs x manifests) storage reads. On remote storage
(GCS/S3) with many tags this throttles GC to tens of seconds per
deleted blob and keeps the repo lock held for hours, blocking pushes:
a repo with 519 manifests took ~20s per blob (~500 sequential manifest
GETs each), turning a single cleanup into a multi-day run.

Build the referenced-blob set once per CleanupRepo call and refresh it
only after a manifest deletion rewrites index.json. The per-blob check
is preserved for the DeleteBlob API path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Sebastian Thees <thees@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(gc): address review comments on referenced-blob collection

Follow-up to the CleanupRepo optimization, addressing PR #4236 review
feedback:

- collectReferencedBlobs now dedups via a shared visited set, so a
  manifest digest shared by multiple tags is traversed only once
  instead of being re-read per descriptor.
- collectReferencedBlobs returns an error and skips only missing-blob
  errors (ErrBlobNotFound / PathNotFoundError), propagating any other
  read error (e.g. corrupt manifest JSON) instead of swallowing it, so
  an incomplete referenced set can no longer cause still-referenced
  blobs to be deleted.
- CleanupRepo falls back to the per-blob IsBlobReferenced check when the
  referenced set is unavailable (initial build or post-manifest-delete
  refresh fails) instead of treating every blob as unreferenced.

Tests cover shared-digest read-once, missing-blob skip, corrupt-manifest
error propagation, and the per-blob fallback on both the initial-build
and refresh failure paths.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Sebastian Thees <thees@users.noreply.github.com>

* refactor(gc): make orphan-blob cleanup GC-owned

Following review feedback on #4236, move the "what is referenced?" policy
fully into the GC package and reduce imagestore's CleanupRepo to a plain
blob-delete helper.

- gc.removeUnreferencedBlobs now builds the complete referenced-blob set
  once per repo via common.GetReferencedBlobs and filters orphans from it,
  replacing the shallow addIndexBlobsToReferences pass (removed together
  with addImageIndexBlobsToReferences/addImageManifestBlobsToReferences).
- common.collectReferencedBlobs now also traverses docker-compat
  manifest-list/manifest media types, so schema2 multi-arch configs and
  layers are collected instead of being dropped (they were previously
  missed by the shallow GC helper).
- CleanupRepo deletes the passed, already-filtered orphan blobs without a
  second index walk, and the ErrBlobReferenced -> deleteImageManifest +
  refresh fallback is removed (unreachable on the GC path).
- cleanRepo now prunes index.json descriptors with an unknown/unsupported
  media type before blob GC, so such entries and their blobs are collected
  together instead of orphaning the config/layers behind a dangling entry.
- GC dry-run is now fully non-destructive: blob and upload GC are skipped
  under DryRun, matching the already-gated index update.

Tests cover docker-compat collection, multi-arch config/layer retention,
shared-manifest read-once, unknown-media-type pruning, and dry-run safety.

* fix(storage): fail closed on blob-reference check errors

IsBlobReferencedInImageIndex discarded the errors from its recursive
index traversal and from isBlobReferencedInImageManifest (found, _ = ...),
so a non-not-found read error (corrupt JSON, permission, partial read) on a
nested manifest/index made it return (false, nil) — reporting a still
referenced blob as unreferenced and allowing its deletion. It now propagates
those errors, matching collectReferencedBlobs; genuinely missing blobs
(ErrBlobNotFound / PathNotFound) are still skipped.

On the single-blob delete path, deleteBlob dropped the IsBlobReferenced
error (ok, _ := ...), so a reference-check failure defaulted ok to false and
the blob was deleted with unknown reference status. The shared
deleteBlobChecked predicate is widened func() bool -> func() (bool, error) so
deleteBlob fails closed (returns the error, does not delete); CleanupRepo's
always-false predicate is unchanged (GC still deletes its pre-filtered orphan
set). The DeleteImageManifest index guard likewise stops discarding its
IsBlobReferencedInImageIndex error.

Adds tests for the nested error-propagation paths and the deleteBlob
fail-closed behavior, asserts the not-found skip is preserved, and repairs
three s3 dedupe-deferred tests whose mocks never populated a valid index.json
(the old fail-open behavior masked the resulting ErrRepoBadVersion).

fix(gc): prevent exponential nested-index walks during untagged GC; correctly GC multi-tag and cosign referrers that share a digest (#4318)

* fix(gc): visit each index digest once in untagged/referrer walks

Duplicate or shared nested index digests made identifyManifestsReferencedInIndex
and removeReferrersWithMissingSubject (formerly removeIndexReferrers) re-fetch and
recurse per path (O(2^N)), holding the store lock for the whole CleanRepo pass.
Add a seen-set so each digest is walked at most once (O(distinct objects)),
matching collectReferencedBlobs / GetReferrers.

Signed-off-by: Andrei Aaron <andreifdaaron@gmail.com>

* refactor(gc): distinguish remove (index refs) from delete (storage)

Rename helpers so method names match behavior: remove* drops references
from indexes (and syncs metaDB), delete* removes objects from storage.
gcManifest becomes removeManifestIfOlderThan; removeUnreferencedBlobs /
removeBlobUploads become deleteUnreferencedBlobs / deleteBlobUploads.

Signed-off-by: Andrei Aaron <andreifdaaron@gmail.com>

* fix(gc): finish multi-tag/cosign referrer GC; keep StatBlob fail-closed

Behavior changes:
- Orphaned-referrer GC walks only root index.json rows (no nested-index
  recursion) and visits every sibling, including multi-tag and cosign
  entries that share a digest.
- removeManifestIfOlderThan deletes by tag when present so duplicate-digest
  siblings no longer hit ErrManifestConflict and leave GC stuck.
- After a subject-path delete, skip the legacy cosign tag path so a second
  delete does not return ErrManifestNotFound and abort mid-pass.
- Hard Get failures in the referrer walk skip that row and continue so stale
  prune and blob/upload cleanup can still run.
- identifyManifestsReferencedInIndex still soft-continues on missing Get
  (same as main) but fails closed on other read errors to avoid under-marking
  referenced manifests.
- isBlobOlderThan stays fail-closed on any StatBlob error (same as main):
  ImageStore collapses transient S3/network Stat failures into
  ErrBlobNotFound, so treating "missing" as GC-eligible would risk deleting
  live index rows. removeManifest soft-ignores ErrManifestNotFound.

Signed-off-by: Andrei Aaron <andreifdaaron@gmail.com>

fix(storage): honor docker2s2 compat media types in delete/prune/scrub (#4327)

IsBlobReferencedInImageIndex, GetReferencedBlobs, and

manifests as OCI-index/manifest-equivalent via IsImageIndexMediaType/

- UpdateIndexWithPrunedImageManifests and PruneImageManifestsFromIndex

  prune from, or a docker manifest as a prune candidate.
- deleteImageManifest (imagestore.go) didn't guard a digest-delete of
  a docker manifest/manifest-list against still being referenced by a
  parent docker manifest-list, the same way it does for OCI.
- scrubManifest and CheckManifestAndConfig (scrub.go) only recognized

  own independent media-type guard, which would otherwise still reject
  every docker manifest even after the switch recognized it.

Added coverage mirroring the existing OCI-only tests for each path,
verified each new test fails without its corresponding fix and passes

feat(sync): add manifestCheckInterval to throttle on-demand upstream manifest checks (#4328)

* feat(sync): add manifestCheckInterval to throttle on-demand upstream manifest checks

With onDemand enabled, every request for a tag validates the manifest against
upstream, because a tag is mutable. When pulls are frequent and upstream rarely
changes, that is one upstream request per pull even though the image is already
synced locally.

manifestCheckInterval, configured per registry, sets the minimum interval between
upstream checks for the same repo:reference. While the interval has not elapsed
since the last successful check, a locally present manifest is served without
contacting upstream, making already synced images effectively local. The default
of 0 keeps the current behaviour.

The last check time is kept in a map guarded by a mutex, with entries dropped
lazily on lookup and swept in an amortized pass from MarkChecked, so the map stays
bounded to the references seen within the interval without a background goroutine
to own and shut down.

Periodic sync always checks upstream and only refreshes the timestamp, and
requests by digest are unaffected since a locally present digest is already
served without a sync.

Signed-off-by: dongshuzhao <dongshuzhao@baidu.com>

feat(sync): make upstream request concurrency/rate configurable (#4322)

* feat(sync): make upstream request concurrency/rate configurable

Sync shares a single RegClient across all on-demand pulls, and regclient
throttles per upstream host to ReqConcurrent=3 by default. When one zot
proxies many concurrent on-demand pulls of different images from a single
upstream, this cap serializes requests: small manifest lookups queue behind
large blob transfers, showing up as slow manifest responses even when
bandwidth is plentiful.

Expose two optional per-registry knobs so operators can raise the cap:

  - reqConcurrent (*int):    max in-flight requests to the upstream and its
                             mirrors; unset keeps regclient's default (3)
  - reqPerSec (*float64):    max request rate to the upstream and its
                             mirrors; unset keeps regclient's default
                             (0, i.e. unlimited)

Both are applied to the upstream hostConfig in newClient(); mirrors inherit
them via the existing hostConfig copy. Pointer types keep the fields
optional so existing configs are unaffected. validateSync() rejects
non-positive values, and both are documented in examples/.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: 严申 <shen.yan@shiyak.com>

* feat(sync): address review on reqConcurrent/reqPerSec

  validateSyncContent to bring cyclomatic complexity under the gocyclo limit.
- Reject non-finite reqPerSec (NaN, +/-Inf) via invalidOptionalPositiveFloat;
  a naive `<= 0` check lets NaN through. Add a YAML-based verify test covering
  .nan/.inf/-.inf.
- Clarify that reqConcurrent/reqPerSec are per-host caps applied independently
  to the upstream and each mirror (not a shared total) in config.go, service.go
  and examples/README.md.

fix(sync): add disableHTTP2 option to saturate high-bandwidth links (#4335)

* fix(sync): add disableHTTP2 option to saturate high-bandwidth links

net/http multiplexes every request to a host onto a single HTTP/2
connection, so reqConcurrent-style concurrency cannot open more TCP
connections and all traffic shares one congestion window. Add a
per-registry disableHTTP2 config option that forces HTTP/1.1 (pinning
ALPN, not just clearing TLSNextProto) so concurrent requests each get
their own connection, plus a maxIdleConnsPerHost override so those
connections get pooled instead of closed after Go's default of 2.

perf: drop the index walk on blob Content-Type (#4350)

* perf: drop the index walk on blob Content-Type

HEAD/GET on a blob resolved the response Content-Type through
GetBlobDescriptorFromRepo, which reads index.json and then fetches
every manifest in the repo until it finds the digest. That is
O(manifests) storage reads per request, and on a remote driver it
dominates the response: roughly 0.145s per manifest, so minutes on a
repo with several hundred tags (#4344).

Content-Type is not specified for blob pulls. The dist-spec requires
it for manifest pulls only, and the helper already fell back to
application/octet-stream whenever the lookup failed, so the walk only
ever upgraded a header that nothing is entitled to depend on.

Blob responses now always advertise application/octet-stream, which
stays non-empty and parseable for consumers such as
stargz-snapshotter. Manifest media-type resolution is untouched. This
reverts the blob half of #4325; the tests that pinned the descriptor
type now assert the constant and additionally fail if the blob path
reads the index at all.

perf: walk storage once per dedupe run (#4351)

* perf: list storage once per dedupe run

The dedupe and restore task generator called GetNextDigestWithBlobPaths
once per digest, and each of those calls walks the whole storage root to
return a single digest. That is O(digests * full listing): on a remote
driver the startup walk runs for hours, and because the generator holds
the read lock while walking and RunDedupeForDigest then waits for the
write lock, client requests queue for the length of each listing. Blob
HEADs measured 20-23s against Azure Blob throughout, while the dedupe
work itself took about 15ms per digest.

BlobPathsByDigest groups every blob path by digest using one
blobs-directory listing per repository, via GetAllBlobs and BlobPath.
The generator does this on the first Next() of a run and iterates the
result; Reset() clears it so the next run lists again.

Not walking the storage root also avoids a hazard: drivers such as GCS
report an empty or concurrently removed nested prefix as
PathNotFoundError, which aborts a walk part way through (see
pkg/storage/gcs/nextrepo_walk_abort_test.go). Caching such a result
would let a run report itself complete having skipped blobs. GetAllBlobs
treats a missing blobs directory as empty for that one repository, so it
cannot curtail the whole listing.

Refs #4349.

Signed-off-by: Paul Kennedy <9027062+datadot@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: tolerate blobs deleted after the listing

The dedupe and restore tasks act on a listing taken once at the start of
a run, so a blob can be deleted between the listing and the task. Both
loops returned on the first failed Stat, and getOriginalBlobFromDisk
gave up its search for a surviving copy the same way.

Failing the task there is worse than skipping: the scheduler does not
retry failed tasks and their completion callback never runs, so
OnRunComplete never fires. A restore run then never writes its
restore-complete marker and rescans on every startup, and a dedupe run
leaves the deferred-delete gate armed indefinitely.

All three sites now skip a path that has gone and carry on. Real I/O
errors still fail the digest. Restore still requires a surviving content
source, since getOriginalBlob continues to error when no copy holds the
content.

Refs #4349.

Signed-off-by: Paul Kennedy <9027062+datadot@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: skip blobs with an invalid digest filename

GetAllBlobs builds a digest from every filename under blobs/<alg>/
without validating it, where the walk this replaces skipped malformed
names. A stray file would therefore become a task that cannot succeed:
it fails in checkCacheBlob, and a failed task never runs its completion
callback, so OnRunComplete never fires and the restore marker or the
deferred-delete gate stays stuck.

The skip goes in BlobPathsByDigest rather than GetAllBlobs, so GC keeps
validating at its own caller and its current behaviour is unchanged.

Refs #4349.

Signed-off-by: Paul Kennedy <9027062+datadot@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: no-op restore when every listed blob is gone

Skipping missing paths individually was not enough for restore. When
every path in the listing has gone, for instance because the repository
was removed, getOriginalBlobFromDisk still ends at ErrBlobNotFound and
restoreDedupedBlobs fails before reaching the per-path skip. A failed
task never runs its completion callback, so OnRunComplete stays blocked.

There is nothing to restore in that case, so it is now a no-op. A
placeholder that still exists with no content source anywhere continues
to fail: leaving it zero-size while the restore-complete marker is
written would suppress the scan that would otherwise notice.

anyBlobExists treats a path that has gone as absent and anything else,
such as a permission error, as present, so a real I/O problem is not
mistaken for a deleted blob.

Refs #4349.

Signed-off-by: Paul Kennedy <9027062+datadot@users.noreply.github.com>

fix(cve): stop SBOM generation from widening CVE results (#4366)

Turning on the trivy sbom config also turned on comprehensive detection
priority, --removed-pkgs and --include-dev-deps. One Trivy report feeds both
the SBOM and the CVE API, so enabling SBOMs quietly changed which CVEs zot
reports.

Comprehensive detection is the main problem. It stops Trivy filtering files
owned by the OS package manager, so those files get scanned a second time as
language packages and matched against NVD. Distros that backport fixes then
look vulnerable when they are not.

Scanning redhat/ubi9 this way adds 14 CVEs that Red Hat has already patched,
such as CVE-2022-40897 and CVE-2023-32681. redhat/ubi10 goes from 0 to 7,
since Trivy ships no Red Hat advisory data for RHEL 10 at all.

These three settings are now separate config options, off by default:

  detectionPriority  (--detection-priority, defaults to "precise")
  scanRemovedPkgs    (--removed-pkgs)

fix(meta): release the repo quota slot when a repo is emptied (#4332)

fix(meta,storage): remove emptied repos from storage and metadb

storage.maxRepos is enforced against metaDB.CountRepos(), but no code
path removed a repo's meta record on delete, and GC removed repo
layouts without touching metadb. The count therefore never decreased:
once a registry reached maxRepos, pushes creating new repositories
were rejected until restart, and a layout GC reaped left a stale key
that let a later push to the same name skip the limit.

Layout removal now happens in one place, a storage-only
ImageStore.RemoveIdleRepository(repo, maxBlobAge), which deletes the
repo directory once it holds no manifests, no blob uploads and no
blobs, and reports whether it did. The orchestrators that already hold
both handles then delete the meta record iff the layout was removed,
so storage stays free of any MetaDB dependency:

- OnDeleteManifest (hooks) calls it with a zero max blob age, so a
  repo emptied by manifest deletes is reclaimed immediately, orphan
  blobs included, then drops the meta record; a meta delete failure
  is logged, and ParseStorage heals the stale record on restart.
- The referrers-tag and expected signature-miss paths
  (ErrImageMetaNotFound after the subject was already removed) no
  longer skip the release: deleting the last leftover signature frees
  the layout and the quota slot instead of leaking both until restart.
- cleanRepo (GC) calls it with the configured GC delay after blob
  reaping, so GC removes repos it emptied, and also blobless empty
  layouts, which the old removeRepo predicate (len(gcBlobs) > 0)
  never removed, then drops the meta record, logging instead of
  aborting the rest of the pass on a meta failure.
- CleanupRepo no longer deletes repo directories, so every layout
  delete goes through RemoveIdleRepository.
- Emptiness is read from the OCI index, not from repo meta: untagged
  content such as a signature referrer leaves no tag behind to count.
- Repos still holding content, and repos with an upload in progress,
  are kept. Dry-run GC removes neither the layout nor the meta record.

Tests (all fail without the change):

- pkg/storage/imagestore: RemoveIdleRepository removes idle layouts,
  orphan blobs included, keeps repos with manifests, uploads or young
  blobs, and no-ops on missing repos; layout-only, no meta assertions.
- pkg/meta (internal): releaseIdleRepository deletes the meta record
  only after a successful layout removal, keeps it when the layout
  stays or the store fails, and swallows a meta delete failure.
- pkg/storage/gc: GC deletes the meta record together with the layout,
  removes blobless empty layouts, and removes neither on a dry run.
- pkg/meta: an emptied repo loses layout and meta; a repo holding
  another tagged manifest, or only an untagged one, keeps both;
  deleting an orphaned signature referrer releases the emptied repo
  instead of surfacing ErrImageMetaNotFound.
- pkg/api: partial delete keeps the slot, full delete releases it and
  drops the repo from _catalog, the emptied name is reusable and
  counts as a new repo under the limit, the release survives a
  restart, and the path holds with GC enabled.
- test/blackbox: the end-to-end form, asserting the catalog no longer
  lists the deleted repo, plus a guard that releasing a slot releases
  only one.

feat(events): configurable CloudEvents source and type namespace (#4385)

The source and every event type are compile-time constants, so each
delivery announces `zotregistry.dev` with types under `zotregistry.*`.
An operator running zot inside a larger service cannot present its own
identity, and a receiver has no way to tell one deployment, or one
tenant, from another: the value is identical for every zot in existence.

Identity carries the two values and falls back to the built-ins, so a
zero value behaves exactly as before. NewRecorder keeps its signature and
delegates; NewRecorderWithIdentity takes the override. TypeOf renames
only the leading namespace, leaving the event itself intact, and a type
outside the built-in namespace is passed through untouched.

Wired to two optional fields on the events config, both empty by default,
so upgrading changes nothing until an operator sets them. A typePrefix
with a leading, trailing or double dot is rejected at config validation,
since it would render event types with empty segments.

feat(events): reload the event recorder on config change (#4400)

The recorder is built once at startup and handed to every image store and
to the CVE scanner, so a config reload never reaches it: new sinks, URLs
and credentials only take effect when the process restarts. accessControl
and htpasswd already reload, which makes the events extension the odd one
out, and on Kubernetes it is what still forces a pod roll when a webhook
is created, rotated or repaired.

Put the recorder behind a wrapper that guards it with a read-write lock.
Every consumer is handed the wrapper once, so replacing the delegate
reaches all of them without touching an emit site. The read side is held
across the whole forwarded call, so once a swap returns nothing can still
be inside the delegate it handed back and closing it is safe. A nil
delegate records nothing, which is how a build or a configuration without
events already behaves, and is what lets a reload enable events on a
server that started without them. Close goes out through the same
detach: it swaps the delegate out before closing it, so a call already
inside has returned, and dispatched its publish, before the sinks it was
publishing to are torn down.

LoadNewConfig rebuilds and swaps when the events config changed, closing
the recorder it replaced. Sinks are live connections, so this rebuilds
rather than re-reads, and only when the config actually moved: whether it
did is answered by EventsFingerprint, alongside the storage fingerprint
that already serves the same purpose, so an unrelated edit does not tear
down open connections. The fingerprint compared against is the one the
installed recorder was built from and it only advances after a successful
swap, so a rebuild that failed on something temporary is retried when the
same config comes back rather than looking like it had been applied. The
config package otherwise only learns to carry Extensions.Events across a
reload, in the same shape as the sync and scrub extensions beside it.

Replacing a recorder makes three existing rough edges reachable, so all
are fixed here. Publishing dispatches asynchronously, so closing a
replaced recorder could tear a sink down while an event was still going
out to it; the recorder now tracks in-flight publishes and Close waits
for them. Building a recorder returned on the first bad sink without
closing the ones already opened, which leaked a connection on every
failed reload; the sinks built so far are now closed before returning.
And the HTTP sink's Close was a no-op even though each sink clones its
own transport, so a sink dropped by a reload kept its pooled connections,
and their goroutines, alive for the life of the process; it now releases
them.

Shutdown closes the recorder once the scheduler and the server have
drained, so the sinks a reload made worth closing are also released when
the process goes down rather than dropped with it. Closing is terminal:
a reload still in flight when shutdown wins the swap gets its recorder
handed straight back instead of installed, so the caller closes it and
it cannot be left live behind a wrapper nobody closes again.

Tests cover the wrapper (each event kind counted on its own method, swap,
enable, disable, close, a nil and a zero value wrapper, publishing
concurrently with a swap, and that a swap and a close each wait for a
call already inside the delegate), that Close waits for a publish still
in flight and detaches what it closed, that closing an HTTP sink drops
the connection it pooled, that a sink opened before a later one fails is
closed again, the fingerprint, and LoadNewConfig itself against live
receivers: deliveries move between them, enabling by reload starts
delivery and disabling stops it, an unchanged config keeps the existing
sinks rather than redialling them, an image store handed the recorder at
startup follows the swap, and a rebuild that fails leaves the previous
recorder delivering, and that shutdown closes and detaches the recorder.
They fail without the reload wiring.

Signed-off-by: Bachir Khiati <bachir.khiati@gmail.com>

fix(cli): reload config on Kubernetes ConfigMap updates (#4384)

The config hot reloader watched only the config file and reacted only to
Write events. A Kubernetes ConfigMap or Secret mount never produces one:
kubelet's AtomicWriter writes a new payload directory and atomically
retargets the ..data symlink, so the watched inode is deleted and the
watch dies silently. Config changes, accessControl edits included, were
never applied until the pod restarted.

Keep watching the file itself for in-place writes and add a periodic
stat fingerprint check (identity, size, mtime) as the guarantee: it
catches whatever the watch cannot see. A replacement is left entirely to
the poll, which re-adds the watch to the inode that replaced the retired
one; write events are debounced because editors deliver them in bursts.

Since the poll carries reloads on its own, fsnotify becomes optional
rather than required. A watcher that cannot be created no longer fails
startup: the reloader keeps a nil watcher and selects over nil channels,
as the htpasswd watcher does, so a host out of inotify instances reloads
at poll latency instead of refusing to boot. The fingerprint baseline is
taken when the reloader is built rather than when it starts, so a config
replaced while the controller is still initialising is still seen as a
change instead of being adopted as the baseline and lost.

After a reload, fields that still differ between the file and the
effective configuration are compared unmasked and logged at warn level:
sanitizing both sides turns a rotated secret into the same mask on each
and hides a change that needs a restart, and only the field paths are
ever logged. The unmasked side comes from SnapshotJSON, which serializes
under the config lock: a view for comparison rather than a clone, since
what JSON does not carry is absent from it: the reload applies
only the reloadable subset, so anything left over needs a restart, and
an operator editing a ConfigMap deserves to see that rather than assume
the reload covered it.

Two adjacent fixes the tests turned up:

- the credentials file is followed nil-safely across every LDAP
  transition (moved, newly enabled, removed), where before removing the
  ldap section panicked the reloader and adding one left the file
  unwatched. An ldap section enabled by reload has no client built at
  startup, so the auth path guards against it and the reload, rather
  than every request reaching that guard, warns that a restart is
  needed. A reload also names the ldap settings it cannot apply: only
  the bind credentials reach the live client, so an address, port,
  baseDN or caCert change lands in the config while the client keeps
  serving with the old one, which the field diff cannot see because both
  sides already agree. The client records the caCert path its pool was
  built from, since the pool itself cannot be compared to a path.
- an invalid config no longer re-reads on every poll tick; the failed
  file is fingerprinted so the next real change retries, and the failure
  is logged through the controller's logger so it reaches the operator's
  configured output. A load that failed on its credentials file
  fingerprints the path it decoded, so creating that file retries
  instead of leaving the config stranded behind fingerprints that no
  longer move; it is a slot of its own, so a config that failed for an
  unrelated reason keeps tracking the credentials the running config
  still authenticates against.

A poll that lands inside the debounce window opened by a write cancels
that pending timer before reloading, so one edit cannot reload twice and
restart every background task a second time.

The reloader logs through the controller's logger rather than one of its
own, so reload lines honour the configured level and output instead of
going to a second sink at a fixed level. Creating the watcher can no
longer fail the constructor, so it returns the reloader alone.

Also: Stop waits for the watcher loop, so an in-flight reload cannot
overlap the controller shutdown that follows it.

Tests cover the kubelet AtomicWriter layout (payload directory plus
atomic symlink retarget), the restart-required warning, every LDAP
transition including a request that must not panic, and the invalid
config retry, the reloader running with no watcher at all, and a change
landing before Start not being adopted as the baseline.
examples/kind/kind-config-reload.sh runs the whole
scenario on a kind cluster, replacing a ConfigMap to grant a second user
access and asserting the change lands live with zero pod restarts; a
nightly workflow job runs it.
